verdicts.title: On Proof Complexity of Resolution over Polynomial Calculus
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The proof system Res (PCd,R) is a natural extension of the Resolution proof system that instead of disjunctions of literals operates with disjunctions of degree d multivariate polynomials over a ring R with Boolean variables. Proving super-polynomial lower bounds for the size of Res(PC1,R)-refutations of Conjunctive normal forms (CNFs) is one of the important problems in propositional proof complexity. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns size-width relations and lower bounds for Res(PCd, R) refutations of Tseitin/Flow/random/PHP formulas via algebraic proof systems, with no mention of effective resistance, Laplacian pseudoinverse, or any electrical-network metric bounding DPLL/tree-resolution size on 3-regular graphs.

verdicts.title: Bounded-depth Frege complexity of Tseitin formulas for all graphs
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We prove that there is a constant K such that Tseitin formulas for an undirected graph G requires proofs of size 2twpGq Ωp1{dq in depth-d Frege systems for d ă K logn log logn , where twpGq is the treewidth of G. This extends H̊astad recent lower bound for the grid graph to any graph. Furthermore, we prove tightness of our bound up to a multiplicative constant in the top exponent. It shares the Tseitin framework but does not interact with the specific charged-pair resistance claim.
